name: RGB-D benchmark datasets
description: The advent of the Microsoft Kinect three years ago stimulated not only the computer vision community for new algorithms and setups to tackle well-known problems in the community but also sparked the launch of several new benchmark datasets to which future algorithms can be compared 019 to. This review of the literature and industry developments concludes that the current RGB-D benchmark datasets can be useful to determine the accuracy of a variety of applications of a single or multiple RGB-D sensors.
typical_sota_score: varies widely by task and dataset (e.g., classification tasks often report 85–99% accuracy; detection/segmentation/pose results typically range ~60–90%), not directly comparable across different RGB‑D tasks
reputation: An early and influential family of benchmarks that helped establish RGB-D sensing as a standard evaluation setting in computer vision.
notes: Older non-LLM vision benchmark review; results vary widely by task and dataset, and many constituent datasets are now dated.
